significance.root_decision: Both characterizations of Conjecture 31 hold for every finite ordered matching. The content is part (i): with the vertex order fixed, deciding a 1-stack 1-queue layout is a 2-SAT problem, whose contradiction cycles can be arbitrarily long, so 2-SAT alone gives no finite obstruction set. The proof shows that for intervals, three-edge forcing configurations plus propagation decide colourability, and that the geometry of intervals shortens every contradiction path to at most one link. Hence every matching without such a layout contains one with at most six edges, and an enumeration of the 11,465 matchings with at most six edges gives exactly the 12 patterns of Figure 19a. Part (ii) is routine (a failure needs a crossing pair and a nesting pair, at most four edges; also the source's Lemma 27). Lean defines ordered matchings on natural-number endpoints, layouts as the source does, and containment as an injective edge map preserving every endpoint comparison; the figure patterns are literal endpoint tables; no size cap enters the statement.
significance.caveat: Modest result: the new argument for part (i) is about a page and a half of elementary interval geometry plus a finite enumeration, and part (ii) is routine; the cross-model reviewer puts 0.60 on a specialist calling part (i) not routine. ProbXiv (HTTP 402), MathSciNet and zbMATH were not checked. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the final theorem and every definition it uses with the endpoint the Claude Opus reviewer had written (identical), and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check compared the definitions and all 20 pattern tables with the source's Figure 19.
